about: Sourced life stories for the prophets of the eighth century (Amos, Hosea, Micah and Joel; Isaiah's story is in prophets-exile.json). Written from Scripture and the dossier Research/People/prophets-eighth-century.md.

amos-amo-1-1.short: A herdman of Tekoa in Judah, sent by the LORD to prophesy to Israel in the days of Uzziah and Jeroboam son of Joash.

paragraphs.text: Amos was “among the herdmen of Tekoa”. His book dates his words to the days of Uzziah king of Judah and of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, “two years before the earthquake”. The book of Zechariah also recalls how the people fled “from before the earthquake in the days of Uzziah king of Judah”.

Amos told how he came to prophesy: “I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet's son; but I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit: And the LORD took me as I followed the flock, and the LORD said unto me, Go, prophesy unto my people Israel.”

His words open with “The LORD will roar from Zion”, and go on against Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, Ammon and Moab, then Judah, and then Israel. He said a prophet could not keep silent: “the Lord GOD hath spoken, who can but prophesy?”

He told of visions the Lord showed him. When he saw locusts eating the grass of the land, he prayed, “O Lord GOD, forgive, I beseech thee: by whom shall Jacob arise? for he is small”; when he saw fire, he prayed, “O Lord GOD, cease, I beseech thee”. Both times “The LORD repented for this”. Then he saw the Lord with a plumbline, a basket of summer fruit, and the Lord standing upon the altar.

Amaziah the priest of Beth-el sent word to King Jeroboam that “Amos hath conspired against thee”, and told Amos to flee into the land of Judah and prophesy there, “But prophesy not again any more at Beth-el: for it is the king's chapel”. Amos answered him with a word from the LORD against Amaziah and his house. Scripture does not say whether Amos then left, or how his life ended.
In Acts, Stephen and James both quote words from his book, Stephen as “written in the book of the prophets”, without naming Amos.

hosea-hos-1-1.short: Hosea son of Beeri, told by the LORD to take “a wife of whoredoms”; he married Gomer, and her children's names carried the LORD's word to Israel.

paragraphs.text: The word of the LORD came to Hosea the son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.

“The beginning of the word of the LORD by Hosea” was a command: “Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms: for the land hath committed great whoredom, departing from the LORD.” So he took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim.

Gomer bore him a son, and the LORD said, “Call his name Jezreel”. She bore a daughter, to be called Lo-ruhamah, “for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel”, and after weaning her she bore a son, to be called Lo-ammi, “for ye are not my people”. Then the names were turned round: “Say ye unto your brethren, Ammi; and to your sisters, Ru-hamah.”

Later the LORD told him, “Go yet, love a woman beloved of her friend, yet an adulteress”. He bought her “for fifteen pieces of silver” and a homer and a half of barley, and told her, “Thou shalt abide for me many days”. The text does not name her.

The rest of his book is the word he spoke to Israel and Ephraim, beginning “Hear the word of the LORD, ye children of Israel” and ending “O Israel, return unto the LORD thy God”. Scripture tells nothing of his later life or his death.

Paul quotes him by name: “As he saith also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people”. Matthew, without naming him, quotes “Out of Egypt have I called my son”, words from Hosea's book.

micah-jer-26-18.short: Micah the Morasthite, who prophesied concerning Samaria and Jerusalem in the days of Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

paragraphs.text: “The word of the LORD that came to Micah the Morasthite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, which he saw concerning Samaria and Jerusalem.” Scripture names no father for him and tells little of his life.

In his book he says he will mourn for Samaria's wound, which had come to Judah: “I will wail and howl, I will go stripped and naked”. Against prophets who cried “Peace” he said, “But truly I am full of power by the spirit of the LORD”.
He said that for the sins of its rulers “shall Zion for your sake be plowed as a field, and Jerusalem shall become heaps”.

Later, in the reign of Jehoiakim, when Jeremiah was on trial for his life, certain elders of the land recalled that “Micah the Morasthite prophesied in the days of Hezekiah king of Judah” these words, and asked, “Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him at all to death? did he not fear the LORD, and besought the LORD, and the LORD repented him of the evil which he had pronounced against them?”
When Herod asked where Christ should be born, the chief priests and scribes answered, “In Bethlehem of Judaea: for thus it is written by the prophet”, and quoted words close to those in Micah's book.

joel-jol-1-1.short: Joel the son of Pethuel, to whom the word of the LORD came; Scripture tells nothing more of his life.

paragraphs.text: “The word of the LORD that came to Joel the son of Pethuel.” His book names no king and gives no date, and Scripture says nothing else about him.
His book calls the old men and all the inhabitants of the land to hear of a plague of locusts, and calls the priests to lament: “Sanctify ye a fast, call a solemn assembly”.
On the day of Pentecost Peter said, “But this is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel”, and quoted Joel's words about the LORD's spirit poured out upon all flesh.
